scope: All 36 requested work items. Implemented slices do not imply complete subsystem support.

architecture_decision.current: Windows x64 runs Intel guests directly; keep it as the regression baseline.
architecture_decision.preferred_next: Native Windows ARM64 port, conditional on an available ARM64 host and ABI probes.
architecture_decision.alternative: ARM64-to-x64 dynarec is a separate backend if the x64-host requirement is retained.
architecture_decision.memory_ordering: Measure guest atomic ordering. Apple's Rosetta TSO control is not assumed available on Windows ARM hardware.

phases.name: Evidence, contracts and debugging
phases.exit_gate: Same-artifact Mac/Adapter comparisons with complete case IDs; versioned ABI contracts; guest-PC, registers and instruction-step evidence.

phases.name: Loaders and language runtimes
phases.exit_gate: Measured shared-cache images, ObjC/Swift consumers, cross-image unwinding and Mach VM error/lifetime probes.

phases.name: System services and Foundation
phases.exit_gate: Reference-matched queues/runloops, complex IPC, process behavior and real service consumers; preserve existing broker regressions.

phases.name: Graphics and desktop UI
phases.exit_gate: NSWindow hello-world with observed drawing, input, pasteboard and orderly teardown; resource/shader tests before claiming graphics coverage.

phases.name: ARM64 and arm64e execution
phases.exit_gate: Pinned ARM64 CLI and architecture litmus probes; 16K guest-page semantics; authenticated-pointer tests separately from plain ARM64.

phases.name: Xcode integration
phases.exit_gate: Pass each of M0 through M4 with the actual named executable and a retained trace/output artifact.

phases.name: Instruments, devices and Simulator
phases.exit_gate: Measured DTX/device pairing conversations and actual device tests; Simulator remains deferred until prior Xcode gates pass.

items.name: Real macOS reference execution
items.work: Hosted Intel Mac reference executed successfully (run39667131995); compressed native capture, OS/build and exact executable hash retained. Physical device/GPU/desktop traces remain separate.

items.name: Differential harness: thousands of probes
items.work: Three same-artifact suites match a hosted Intel Mac in debug and release: 4096 libc cases (after correcting strtol no-conversion errno and timegm pre-1900 rejection), 4096 Objective-C cases over eight dispatch/metadata families (after the Darwin capture disproved an isa-inclusive instance-size assumption) 1024 threading cases over create/join, mutex, once, TLS keys, condition handoff, attributes and return values, and 30 whole-program cases over the pinned jq 1.8.2 and ripgrep 15.2.0 artifacts (stdout/stderr/exit status). Expand to services (Mach, XPC, launchd).

items.name: ARM64 backend decision
items.work: Prefer native Windows ARM64 when hardware is available; retain dynarec as a separately scoped x64-host backend. Neither is implemented.

items.name: Guest crash debugging and single-step
items.work: Nine Windows LLDB tests cover genuine guest UD2, register/disassembly/backtrace capture, relocated symbols, VM breakpoints, instruction step and timeout cleanup, in debug and release; the release hook needed a unique body to survive identical-code folding. Darwin debugserver APIs remain P5.

items.name: Strict subsystem ABI contracts
items.work: Seven versioned subsystem contracts and automated layout/path/symbol-drift checks exist. Extend contracts and native reference coverage with every new subsystem.

items.name: Binary pass/fail milestones
items.work: The five binary gates (M0 NSWindow hello-world, M1 xcodebuild, M2 Xcode welcome window, M3 open project, M4 build project) all require AppKit and Xcode's own GUI binaries, which are Apple artifacts this host cannot obtain or redistribute. Gate definitions and the pass criteria stay recorded; see docs/item-gates.md.

items.name: System image and dyld shared cache
items.work: Acquire identified user-supplied image, extract/rebase caches and subcaches, resolve shared-cache fixups and image lifecycle. Existing XIP extraction is not cache loading.

items.name: Apple-ABI Objective-C runtime
items.work: Raw-isa MRC classes/metaclasses, selectors, inheritance, msgSend/Super2, load/initialize, startup categories and absolute/relative method lists across classic, chained and relative fixup forms, with all 4096 same-binary Objective-C differential cases matching a hosted Intel Mac. Compiler-emitted protocols, adoption, method descriptions and property introspection match a second 4096-record Mac suite in debug/release. Runtime-owned ARC strong/weak ownership, inherited ivar cleanup, custom RR and recognized x64 return handoffs match two 1024-record Mac suites (O0/O2) in debug/release. ARC Blocks, atomic/copy properties, foreign objects, exceptions and dynamic registration remain.

items.name: Swift guest runtime
items.work: Apple Mach-O Swift metadata/refcounting/concurrency/reflection and ObjC interop. Native Windows Swift alone does not satisfy this ABI.

items.name: Darwin compact unwind and DWARF
items.work: Loaded-image unwind lookup, personalities and C++/ObjC exceptions across guest/host frames; distinguish Windows SEH.

items.name: Mach VM emulation
items.work: mach_vm_allocate/deallocate/protect plus the vm_* spellings execute over the host address space with Darwin return codes, a recorded-region rule and a verified Mach-O consumer. Remaining: region queries, sharing, sub-range release, inheritance and ledger accounting.

items.name: 16K guest pages and ARM memory ordering
items.work: Preserve guest alignment/protection/query semantics independently of host page granularity; run atomic litmus tests before choosing ordering adaptations.

items.name: arm64e pointer authentication
items.work: Keys/discriminators/address diversity, signed returns and authenticated fixups. Plain ARM64 or stripping pointer bits is insufficient.

items.name: libdispatch / GCD
items.work: Queues (serial, concurrent, barriers, targets, suspension), sync/async/and_wait, groups, once, after, apply, block objects, timer and user-data sources, the main queue and Block runtime copy/dispose run with verified Mach-O consumers. Remaining: descriptor, process, signal and Mach sources, dispatch_data/io, workloops and QoS scheduling.

items.name: Full CoreFoundation and Foundation
items.work: Current CF strings only; add collections, constant objects, resources, bundles, NSObject lifecycle and toll-free bridging from consumers.

items.name: CFRunLoop on Mach ports
items.work: Modes, sources, observers, timers, wakeups and Mach-port callbacks, with reference ordering.

items.name: Complex Mach messages
items.work: Simple broker messages exist. Add OOL/port descriptors, rights transfer, copy/deallocate rules and partial-failure cleanup.

items.name: XPC
items.work: Typed broker transport exists; Apple interoperability, richer objects, GCD scheduling, peer validation and entitlements remain.

items.name: Real launchd semantics
items.work: Job plist/demand-spawn subset exists. Add domains, KeepAlive, supervision/throttling, socket activation, inherited rights and launchctl behavior.

items.name: fork / exec / posix_spawn
items.work: Start with spawn and argument/environment/descriptor inheritance; model fork snapshots and atfork separately.

items.name: Signals and syscall personality
items.work: Synchronous guest signals: dispositions, masks, pending sets, sigwait, sa_mask and default termination run with a verified Mach-O consumer. Remaining: asynchronous delivery, per-thread masks, siginfo/ucontext, alternate stacks, fault mapping, restart and direct syscall interception.

items.name: IOKit / sysctl / proc_info
items.work: sysctl, sysctlbyname and sysctlnametomib answer about 75 kern/hw/machdep/user/vm names from host facts and fixed Darwin values, and libproc describes the guest's own process, with a verified Mach-O consumer. Remaining: kern.proc and procargs2, net/debug subtrees, disk and performance-level names, other pids, file-descriptor and region flavors, and IOKit.

items.name: macOS service daemons
items.work: cfprefsd, notifyd, distnoted, LaunchServices, securityd/trustd and opendirectoryd binaries are Apple artifacts that are absent from the supplied Xcode XIP and cannot be redistributed; the client side is covered by the launchd and XPC slices. See docs/item-gates.md.

items.name: FSEvents and Spotlight
items.work: Persistent event IDs, rescan/drop semantics, indexing and query behavior; Windows directory notifications are only a backend.

items.name: CoreGraphics / CoreText / CoreAnimation / ImageIO / ColorSync
items.work: Requires Apple framework images and their rendering/text behaviour, which Apple documents only at API level and which this repository may not redistribute; see docs/item-gates.md.

items.name: IOSurface
items.work: Pixel layouts, process sharing, rights, synchronization and host GPU resource interop.

items.name: Metal to D3D12; AIR to DXIL
items.work: Requires Apple's Metal front end that emits AIR; DXC has no AIR front end and no AIR-to-DXIL implementation was identified. See docs/item-gates.md.

items.name: AppKit
items.work: Requires the AppKit framework image and the Cocoa text/responder stack it depends on; see docs/item-gates.md.

items.name: SwiftUI
items.work: Requires Apple's shipping SwiftUI binary, which the Swift compiler repository does not contain; see docs/item-gates.md.

items.name: WindowServer replacement
items.work: Requires WindowServer behaviour and private protocols observable only from a running Mac; see docs/item-gates.md.

items.name: LLDB/debugserver Mach primitives
items.work: Exception ports, task_for_pid, thread_get_state, suspend/resume and memory access. Host LLDB debugging is a separate P0 capability.

items.name: codesign / Security / keychain
items.work: Signature/trust parsing, guest signing/entitlement policy and persistent keychain behavior with test fixtures.

items.name: xcrun / xcode-select / SDK paths
items.work: Developer directory state, tool/SDK discovery, platform/version queries and actual subprocess execution.

items.name: Instruments and DTX services
items.work: Requires Instruments.app and its DTX peer implementation; the Mach message layer is covered by the existing IPC slice. See docs/item-gates.md.

items.name: Physical devices / USB / usbmuxd / CoreDevice / pairing
items.work: Windows transport/drivers, trust records, developer mode and service versions require an actual device acceptance run.

items.name: iOS Simulator / CoreSimulator / iOS runtime
items.work: Defer until earlier Xcode gates pass; automation clients do not replace CoreSimulator or iOS frameworks.

milestones.name: NSWindow hello-world
milestones.acceptance: Actual guest NSWindow appears, draws, receives input and closes cleanly.

milestones.name: xcodebuild
milestones.acceptance: Identified Apple xcodebuild performs version/SDK queries through Adapter; host compiler invocation is not a substitute.

milestones.name: Xcode welcome window
milestones.acceptance: Identified Xcode launcher reaches the interactive welcome window with service/runtime logs.

milestones.name: Open project
milestones.acceptance: Open a pinned small project and reach editor/project state without a fatal unsupported call.

milestones.name: Build project
milestones.acceptance: Build the pinned project, retain the output artifact and compare command/results with the Mac reference.
